steps.text: Brown beef in a Dutch oven over medium high heat until browned; drain off any fat.

Add green pepper and sauté for 3 minutes. Stir in tomato sauce, diced tomatoes with juice, bouillon cubes, brown sugar, salt, black pepper, and soy sauce. Reduce heat to low, cover and simmer for 30 to 45 minutes. Stir in rice and heat through.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Stuffed Pepper Soup
raw_recipe.description: Browned ground beef is combined in this tomato based soup with chopped green peppers, cooked rice, beef bouillon, brown sugar and soy sauce.
raw_recipe.name: Easy Stuffed Pepper Soup

review.reviewBody:
Awesome Awesome Awesome!! This is the best soup ever! Well I did do some things different though. 
I added 
2 onions
1 clove of garlic 
4 green peppers.
1/2 cup ketchup
2 tbsp. worchestershire
1 cup water
I reduced to 1 cup of rice
Also, instead of a can of chopped tomatoes I picked 6 fresh from the garded blanched them and scrunched them into the mixture. 
I know these seem like alot of changes but they are all pretty small after all. I only changed it to reflect the way I actually make stuffed peppers. Again, this stuff is really awesome!

Variations: brown the meat with 1 small onion, drain. Add all ingredients, plus 2 cups water. Substitute worchestire sauce instead of soy sauce. Bring to boil. Then add 1 chopped green and 1 chopped yellow pepper. Cover and simmer for 1 hr or until peppers soft. At very end, add 2 cups cooked BROWN RICE for additional 15-20 min. Oh and by the way, I don't have a Dutch oven so after browning meat and onion, I just transferred to a big pot. EXCELLENT!! Thanks Holly!

Loved this recipe! I was craving stuffed green pepper soup and this hit the spot! I pretty much followed the recipe to a 't' but here are the few changes I made/would make: I substituted soy sauce for Worcestershire sauce. I also only did 1 lb of meat which was more than enough for me but I did 3 bell peppers. I also recommend doing maybe 3 cups of rice. 2 wasn't enough for me. Also, the soup was initially thicker than I'd like so I added beef broth along with the bouillon cubes. DO NOT do like previous reviewers suggested and throw the uncooked rice in in step 3. I did it on my first attempt and it sucked all the moisture out. Great, great recipe!

I love stuffed peppers but hate how much time has to go into them so finding this recipe years ago was a blessing! 
Thankfully I read the reviews before trying it out and after making this soup many times over the years, with different modifications each time, I've got it down to a science! 
With the following modifications, my family and I feel this soup is perfect!

I start off seasoning the ground beef with seasoning salt, onion powder, and garlic powder while browning. (Using 93% makes less grease so I don't bother draining before adding other ingredients.) Instead of beef bouillon cubes, I use 32 oz of beef broth. This makes a 'soupier' consistency. Substitute worcestershire sauce for the soy sauce. 
I also use 3 large green peppers, one just isn't enough! Lastly, to make a heartier soup, I use 3 cups of rice instead of 2, as the original recipe calls for.

We enjoyed this soup a lot. The changes I made were mostly from necessity. I was out of tomato sauce so used an extra can of tomatoes pureed. Used beef broth instead of bouillon, and a red pepper instead of green. Per other reviews I added a little garlic powder, about 1/2 cup of diced onion and 1T of Worcestershire. Cooked my rice with half water half beef broth.

I did some modification and it turned out fantastic. Cut rice in half and added 2c riced cauliflower. Used ground turkey instead of beef. Added the rolice and cauliflower with the rest of ingredients versus waiting until end. Added about 10-14 oz of water to compensate for uncooked rice.

This was allright. To my surprise, my hubs liked this quite a bit (he can be picky at times...). I wasn't a fan for two reasons - this was a tad bland for my liking and WAAY too thick to be considered soup. I even added water. After looking at my stockpot, I knew there was no way this would resemble soup without it.... I suggest adding 1 c. water per boullion cube and DOUBLING the liquid when making a full batch of this. Since I halved everything, I added 2 c. of water / 2 bullion cubes. I also added the full T of W sauce (subbed for soy), sugar and seasonings called for (FYI, I used seasoned salt in lieu of plain table salt). My only other changes were using an entire green bell pepper (didn't see the point in wasting half of one), adding a small, chopped onion and using Italian-seasoned tomatoes / garlic & onion flavored tomato sauce (the latter two to add a flavor boost). I also added my rice in step #3, brought my pot to a boil and then simmered for a half hour. Serving steaming bowlfuls with garlic bread, this was a warming meal on this dreary September day. Thanks for sharing, Holly! :-)

I made this soup.I used ground beef.I browned the beef and
added the garlic,onions and both halves of Green and Yellow
Bell peppers.I added the Bell Peppers when the meat was browned.
I used about six cups water for the soup.I used Ragu Spagehetti
sauce instead of tomato sauce.I used a teaspoon of beef bouillon.
I transfered the hamburger mixture to the soup pot.I added some
kernel corn and green beans.I seasoned the soup with basil and
Oregano and one bay leaf,and 2 tablespoons brown sugar.I used some flour to thicken the soup up.I let the soup cook for about 20 minutes.I cooked the rice by itself.I served with Mozzeralla cheese.
the soup came out perfect.I look forward to making it again.
Its better to serve the soup over the rice.

I really liked this recipe. I made 3 small changes: I used 2 green bell peppers instead of 1, added 1 medium onion (chopped) with the peppers and substituted Worcestershire for the soy sauce. It was a winner & several of my friends asked for the recipe.

I only gave this 4 stars because I had to do 
Mse tweaking for my family's liking...I added about about 2 cloves minced garlic to the ground "beef" (I use ground turkey), reduced the tomato sauce to a 14 ounce can, and used a 14 ounce can each diced and crushed tomatoes as we aren't big cooked tomato people. I added 2 cups beef broth, 2 bouillon cubes and the tomato sauce can full of water (gotta get every last drop!). I also used more green pepper and added the rice to the bowls as I served them

I had to make this soup just as soon as I saw it. I read the reviews and then made my own personal preference changes to it. First, I used the best groung round I can buy as this is a base to this recipe. I browned it with fresh ground pepper and garlic powder. I then roughly diced a med yellow onion, 1 large green pepper, and 1/2 of a med red pepper, and 2 cloves of garlic and added it to the meat just before the meat was completely browned through and continuted browning until veggies were tender. I drained a very small amount of grease, and added 1 tablespoon soy sauce, 2 tablespoons Worcestershire sauce,1 entire 42 oz. bottle of V-8 juice, 3 beef bouillion cubes, 3 cans petite diced tomatoes with juice,1 cup water, the brown sugar, and no salt. I simmered for about 30 -40 minutes, then added only one cup of basmanti rice, which really thickened it up. Next time I will use regular white rice, I think that will stand up better in this soup. I served with a bit of finely grated cheddar cheese on top of everyones bowl and added a slice of garlic bread on the plate and it was a smash hit! This is a recipe that anyone can play with to make it their own, and be a perfect comfort food favorite. It is easy, fairly fast, and a keeper!
I am asked more times for this recipe. Very easy, and you get stuffed peppers without all the fuss.
One of our family's favorite recipes in the wintertime!
Very easy and delicious. I used ground turkey, and added a few chopped carrots and some homemade tomato sauce I needed to use up.
I made this for a group of friends and they loved it and asked me to please share this recipe!
Love this recipe. Everyone in my house likes it.
This is my go-to for stuffed bell pepper soup only change I make is I add some additional hot peppers like habaneros and jalapenos. Super easy tastes great. Easy to freeze for a later day.
This is my family's favorite soup 😄🍲
